adjudicated.jp: 「それより、部活しませんか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "More importantly, shall we have activities?"
adjudicated.assessment: His proposal that they proceed with club activities is preserved despite a formal phrasing choice.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "...well."
adjudicated.assessment: Her hesitant response is functionally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 先輩がじっと見つめてくる。
adjudicated.en: Senpai gazes at me fixedly.
adjudicated.assessment: Her fixed gaze at him is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「手伝いにきてくれたんですか？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Did you come to help me?"
adjudicated.assessment: Her question about whether he came to help is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: 「はあ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Sir!"
adjudicated.assessment: The source is a subdued acknowledgement or noncommittal response. The English changes it into a crisp form of address, altering the speech act and tone.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a subdued acknowledgement such as 'Yeah' or 'Uh-huh.'

adjudicated.jp: 「そうですか」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "So you did."
adjudicated.assessment: Her acceptance of the answer is functionally conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 凝然と、固定された目線が外れない。
adjudicated.en: Her stationary, congealed sight does not move from me.
comments: This being somewhat older writing it's not entirely obvious what Misato's thinking. She seems more troubled about Taichi's ulterior motives than from him coming there at all. Supposing it works since it's Week 1 and that's what readers are supposed to take away, but it doesn't make too much sense holistically (wooo big word). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The stiff diction nevertheless preserves the unbroken, fixed stare.

adjudicated.jp: やがて先輩の顔がふっとほころぶ。
adjudicated.en: Eventually, Senpai's face puffs into the broadest of smiles.
comments: The term also means "to come apart at the seams". Three guesses. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her face gently relaxes or opens into a smile. 'Puffs' gives the wrong physical motion, while 'the broadest' adds an unsupported superlative.
adjudicated.remedy: Describe her face softly relaxing into a smile without the superlative.

highlights.text: puffs into the broadest of smiles

adjudicated.jp: 「ありがとうございます、ぺけくん」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Thank you very much, Peke-kun."
adjudicated.assessment: Her thanks and private form of address are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「いえ、帝国軍人として当然であります」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "'Tis nothing, ma'am, it is the ordinary for a soldier of the Empire."
comments: Ah, Nations of the World. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: He mock-formally says that helping is only natural for an imperial soldier. The English uses the adjective 'ordinary' as a noun and produces an ungrammatical military-register line.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'only natural for a soldier of the Empire' or an equivalent mock-formal expression.

highlights.text: it is the ordinary for a soldier of the Empire

adjudicated.jp: 敬礼。
adjudicated.en: Salute!
adjudicated.assessment: The salute is preserved as a terse action beat.

adjudicated.jp: 彼女はくすくすと笑う。
adjudicated.en: She laughs with a giggle.
adjudicated.assessment: The slightly tautological wording still accurately conveys her quiet giggling laugh.

adjudicated.jp: 「でも残念ですが、今日はもう夜になってしまうのでした」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "It is too bad, but the day has already turned to night."
adjudicated.assessment: She says that the day is about to give way to night, explaining why the activity must end. The English states that night has already arrived, changing the temporal relation.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that it is already going to be night or is getting late.

highlights.text: the day has already turned to night

adjudicated.jp: 「楽しい部活の時間は、おしまい」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "The time for fun club activity is all done."
adjudicated.assessment: Her declaration that the enjoyable club time is over is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「えー」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Eeeh?"
adjudicated.assessment: His drawn-out protest is functionally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「すいませんね、一人でやるって決めていたので、時間は流動的だったりするんです」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Sorry, because I decided to do this on my own, the hours are fluid."
comments: "the decision to do this I took on my own" + "I decided that I must do this alone". -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Despite stiff diction, she explains that the schedule is flexible because she had planned to do the work alone.

adjudicated.jp: 「でも一人じゃ終わらないですよ？　配線だってあるでしょうし」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But alone you cannot finish this, right? There is the wiring."
adjudicated.assessment: He argues that she cannot finish alone and mentions the wiring; both points are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「そもそも電源だって」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "For starters, there is the electricity."
comments: Because the rooftop wouldn't have outlets, not because there's none in the world. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His additional concern about the power supply is functionally conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「平気ですよ」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "It is alright!"
adjudicated.assessment: Her assurance that she will be fine is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「女は度胸です」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Women are pluck."
adjudicated.assessment: She invokes the maxim that a woman needs courage or nerve. The literal predicate construction is unidiomatic and grammatically malformed in English.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'A woman's got to have guts' or another idiomatic courage maxim.

adjudicated.jp: 「じゃ男は愛ですね」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Then men pluck them out."
comments: From "Men are charm, women are pluck", but he took off one kanji so he said "men are love". That doesn't really make sense in English, and the closest thing to this in English (men are from Mars, women are from Venus) doesn't work here. This isn't too far anyway. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His reply says that men are 'love,' creating a deliberate wordplay response to the preceding maxim. The English invents an action of plucking women out and removes the love term entirely.
adjudicated.remedy: Retain the assertion that men are love, with a note or adaptive pun if necessary.

adjudicated.jp: 「先輩、ぼかぁ、ぼかぁ―――」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Senpai, pwease, pwease---"
comments: Childish "boku". It's on Wikipedia and everything(tm). Gah, combo breaker -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: He breaks off while repeating a childish deformation of the first-person pronoun. The English replaces the failed self-reference with an explicit repeated plea that is not in the line.
adjudicated.remedy: Preserve the broken childish 'I—I—' rather than adding a request.

adjudicated.jp: にじり寄ろうとすると、
adjudicated.en: I go to sidle up and,
adjudicated.assessment: His attempt to sidle closer is accurately preserved as a sentence fragment linked to the interruption that follows.

adjudicated.jp: 「部活しゅーりょーっ！」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Cluuub haaas concludeeed!"
adjudicated.assessment: Her elongated emphatic announcement that club activities are over is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「ぐぶぅっ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "G'buh!"
adjudicated.assessment: His compressed cry is functionally represented.

adjudicated.jp: 顔面を片手で突き押され、よりさらに不細工になる俺。
adjudicated.en: With one hand she squeezes on my face, turning me ever more ugly.
comments: Curiously, see CCA0030. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She pushes or shoves his face away with one hand. The English changes the forceful pushing action into squeezing his face.
adjudicated.remedy: Describe her pushing his face away with one hand.

adjudicated.jp: 『ぐぶぅ』とか言っちゃってもうマリアナ海溝の底まで落ちたって感じ。
adjudicated.en: And blurting stuff like that "g'buh" felt like having fallen to the bottom of the Marianas Trench.
comments: See CCB0005. Hum, and CCB2019 too. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His embarrassment over the cry and the Mariana Trench hyperbole are preserved despite awkward syntax.

adjudicated.jp: 「さ、帰りましょう。と言いましても、あなたとわたしは帰る方向も正反対ですけれど、ほほほほ」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "So! Let's go home. And I remind you, that my way home and yours are in the exact opposite direction, hohohohoh!"
comments: She lives just a bit closer to school than Miki. They gotta share like a third of the way. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her invitation to leave, observation that their routes diverge, and theatrical laughter are all preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「……なーんか、釈然としません」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...whaaat, this cannot be fully satisfying!"
comments: For either of them. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The awkward phrasing still conveys his lingering dissatisfaction and inability to accept the outcome.

adjudicated.jp: 「だって、今日はとても楽しかったでしょう？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "But still, today was really fun, was it not?"
adjudicated.assessment: She points out that the day was enjoyable and asks for his agreement; the line is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: 「んー、どうでしょうねー」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Hmmm, was it now..."
adjudicated.assessment: His evasive, drawn-out uncertainty is functionally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「わたしの胸に顔をうずめてる時、お尻触ってましたよね？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "When you were with your face buried in my chest, you were touching my butt, right?"
adjudicated.assessment: Her accusation about what he did while his face was buried against her chest is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silence is exact and uniquely topology-resolved between the bound accusation and the following bound elaboration in the selected source file.

adjudicated.jp: 「ぐにぐにーって、すごい触り方で」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "With plenty of squeeze, and you going all 'squishity-squish!'"
comments: This contradicts facts; we didn't see anything of the sort. Is she making this up, knowing he wouldn't have quite remembered that time, or is the cheating here even stronger than it looks? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her description of his forceful squishing touch is adaptively preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「しかも両手で」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "And furthermore, with both hands."
adjudicated.assessment: Her added detail that he used both hands is exact.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "......"
adjudicated.assessment: The prolonged silence is exact and uniquely topology-resolved between the bound two-handed detail and the following bound reaction in the selected source file.

adjudicated.jp: 「くすぐったかったです」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "And it tickled."
adjudicated.assessment: Her statement that it tickled is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "～♪"
comments: TL Note: ～♪ -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The wordless musical response is exact and uniquely topology-resolved between the bound ticklish admission and the following bound whistle in the selected source file.

adjudicated.jp: あさっての方角に向けて、口笛を吹く。
adjudicated.en: So I whistled when faced with this derailing of thoughts.
comments: PCP CCA0010
adjudicated.assessment: He physically turns toward a completely unrelated direction and whistles, using the idiom 'toward the day after tomorrow.' The English removes the physical direction and replaces it with an abstract derailment of thought.
adjudicated.remedy: Describe him whistling while looking off in a random or unrelated direction.

highlights.text: when faced with this derailing of thoughts

adjudicated.jp: 「オ・ト・コ・ノ・コ、なんですものねー」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Be-ca-use-you-are-a-boooy, are you!"
comments: This is funnier considering "otokonoko" is sort of gaining traction as meaning "transvestite" in contemporary anime parlance (they have one). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She pointedly concludes that this is because he is a boy. The English appends an inverted interrogative tag to the already stated cause, producing the wrong syntax and rhetorical force.
adjudicated.remedy: Use an emphatic assertion such as 'Because you're a boy, after all.'

adjudicated.jp: こめかみのあたりを、ぐりぐりとつつかれる。
adjudicated.en: She drills back and forth right on my temples.
adjudicated.assessment: Her grinding poke at his temples is vividly and accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: けっこう痛い。
adjudicated.en: It's fairly painful.
comments: M. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The considerable pain is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: ごまかせるはずもなかったのだ。
adjudicated.en: I could never swindle my way out of this.
comments: Meaning she sort of knows he's like this, whether she's trolling him or not. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Despite an aggressive verb choice, the English preserves that he has no hope of covering up or talking his way out of the situation.

adjudicated.jp: 「うう……すいません……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ngggh... sorryyy..."
adjudicated.assessment: His pained, drawn-out apology is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「さて、どうしたものやら」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Well then, what am I to do with this."
adjudicated.assessment: Her musing over what to do with him is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「わたしも、そのくらいの価値はある女だったってことですかね」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Would that mean I, myself, am a woman with about that kind of value?"
comments: Misato the traitor. See below: -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She wonders whether the past incident means she was a woman worth that much to him. The English shifts the marked past-tense reflection into a present-tense statement about her general identity.
adjudicated.remedy: Preserve the retrospective 'was a woman worth that much' framing.

highlights.text: am a woman with about that kind of value

adjudicated.jp: 「それともぺけくんが無節操なだけですかねー？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Or is it that you are merely unprincipled, Peke-kun?"
comments: It's not "am I worthless, or are you just a lech?", as it seems on first read; it's "am I worth something, or are you just a lech?" Consider the thing about Taichi being proud of Miki's love despite being what he is. It's ultimately religious, as humans so broken are still loved by God. And so, can Misato being what she is be loved? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her alternative that he is simply indiscriminate and the private address are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「いやいやいや、虚無僧ではありますが無節操などには！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "NoNnoNno, I may be a Komusou, but unprincipled, really!"
comments: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komus%C5%8D -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: He protests that although he may be a komusou, he is not indiscriminate. The ellipsis-dependent Japanese denial is not completed in English, leaving an ungrammatical phrase that can read as an admission of the accusation.
adjudicated.remedy: Complete the denial: 'I may be a komusou, but I'm not indiscriminate.'

adjudicated.jp: 「奴らと同列にされては困ります！！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Putting me side by side with that sort worries me!!!"
adjudicated.assessment: His objection to being lumped together with that group is functionally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 必死に誤魔化す俺の、緊急ギャグは果てしなく寒い。
adjudicated.en: When I'm desperate to deceive, my Emergency Jokes are endlessly lame.
comments: Translation: he's a terrible, terrible, terrible liar. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His desperate cover-up and the hopeless lameness of his emergency joke are accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「ふふふ」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Heh heh heh!"
adjudicated.assessment: Her quiet laugh is functionally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 夕刻の、さらに濃度を増したオレンジを背景に、先輩は体をすこし傾けて、言った。
adjudicated.en: In this evening hour, in this scene where the density of orange grows ever more, Senpai leaned her body just a little and spoke.
adjudicated.assessment: Despite literal color diction, the deepening orange evening backdrop and her slight bodily tilt before speaking are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「許してあげますから、帰って反省タイムです」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "I will forgive you for now, so it is time to go home and reflect."
comments: Works even better in English! Who'd have thunk it. This means both of them, however. She has plenty to reflect on, after all. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her provisional forgiveness and instruction that he go home for reflection time are accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「さようなら、ですよ。ぺけくん」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "This is goodbye, then, Peke-kun."
adjudicated.assessment: Her stylized goodbye and private form of address are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 校舎を出て、屋上を見上げた。
adjudicated.en: I left the school building, and looked up at the rooftop.
adjudicated.assessment: His leaving the building and looking up at the roof are accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: アンテナが立っていた。
adjudicated.en: There the antenna stood.
adjudicated.assessment: The standing antenna is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: その隣。
adjudicated.en: And next to it,
adjudicated.assessment: The fragment locating what follows beside the antenna is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 先輩はまだ、そこにいる。
adjudicated.en: Senpai was, once more, still there,
adjudicated.assessment: Her continued presence there is preserved as the first part of the linked observation.

adjudicated.jp: 作業していた。
adjudicated.en: working, blue collar,
adjudicated.assessment: The source simply says that she was working. The English adds a blue-collar social or occupational characterization that is absent and does not fit the linked sentence.

adjudicated.jp: もうじき夜になるのに。
adjudicated.en: even when it will soon be night,
adjudicated.assessment: The concessive observation that night will soon fall is preserved in the linked sentence.

adjudicated.jp: 一人で。
adjudicated.en: alone.
adjudicated.assessment: The final fragment emphasizing that she remains alone is exactly preserved.

adjudicated.jp: この時になってはじめて。
adjudicated.en: And it was at this moment that, for the first time,
adjudicated.assessment: The delayed realization beginning only at this moment is preserved as a linked fragment.

adjudicated.jp: やんわりと、手伝いを拒絶されたのだと気づいた。
adjudicated.en: I realized that help had been refused, with gentleness.
adjudicated.assessment: Despite stiff syntax, he accurately realizes that his offer of help was gently refused.
